//: Files that must stay byte-identical with the FieldAgent web app. See scripts/mirror.mjs and docs/architecture.md. Formatting is deliberately NOT applied to src/shared (see .prettierignore) - reformatting would break the mirror.

files.why: Due-date maths, due-level thresholds and dashboard assembly. If these drift, the two clients disagree about whether a fire check is overdue.

notYetMirrored.//: Shared in spirit, blocked on a small web-side refactor - see docs/architecture.md.
notYetMirrored.src/lib/cluster.ts: Pure, but type-imports LatLng from geocode.ts, which uses localStorage. Needs LatLng moved to its own module.
notYetMirrored.src/lib/geocode.ts: Caches in localStorage; needs the cache injected rather than assumed.
notYetMirrored.src/lib/types.ts: Contract types are identical, but the queue types carry Blob; mobile stores photo bytes as files on disk.
notYetMirrored.src/lib/sync.ts: buildSubmitBody is pure; the rest imports the web IndexedDB layer.

deliberatelyNotMirrored.//: Ported by hand and allowed to diverge, decided 2026-08-15. Unlike src/shared, none of this is a compliance surface: two clients ordering a list differently is cosmetic, not a wrong answer about whether a check is overdue. Mirroring it would need a refactor in ../fieldagent (its nearby.ts reaches a localStorage-backed geocode cache), which is that repo's call to make.
deliberatelyNotMirrored.src/lib/nearby.ts: Search matching, distance sorting and distance formatting. Close port of the web app's src/lib/nearby.ts, minus its `locate` (which is platform-bound).
deliberatelyNotMirrored.src/lib/geo.ts: haversineKm, verbatim from the web app's cluster.ts.
deliberatelyNotMirrored.src/lib/geocode.ts: postcodes.io lookup. Same protocol, different cache: AsyncStorage here, localStorage there.
deliberatelyNotMirrored.src/lib/cluster.ts: Greedy clustering + nearest-neighbour route order, ported from the web's cluster.ts. Same maths; haversineKm imported from geo.ts here instead of being defined inline.
deliberatelyNotMirrored.src/lib/plan.ts: The assembly half of the web's usePlan hook, extracted to a pure module so it tests without React. Same rounds given the same blocks.
